podcast.title: Nuggets Compilation Release (1972)
podcast.body: Elektra Records was persuaded by guitarist Lenny Kay to release the "Nuggets" compilation in 1972. This double album, which collected material from 1964 to 1968, played a crucial role in memorializing and codifying the entire Garage Rock era. "He was a big fan of this raw and sometimes sloppy rock, and was able to convince electro records to release a collection of material issued between 1964 and 1968."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alt Rock Revivals Part 4: Garage Rock

podcast.title: Box Set Highlights
podcast.body: A box set featuring highlights from Elektra Records over the decades is mentioned. This indicates that record labels themselves can be the subject of comprehensive compilations, celebrating their history and catalog. "Here's one with highlights from Electro Records over the decades."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Dropping The Stooges and Demanding Refund
podcast.body: Elektra Records eventually dropped The Stooges due to the band's escalating drug problems and chaotic live performances. The label went further by demanding an $11,000 refund on an advance they had previously given to the band. "So Electra dropped them. Actually, they more than dropped them. They demanded a refund of $11,000 on an advance they had given the band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About The Stooges?

podcast.title: Extensive Promotional Efforts
podcast.body: Elektra Records backed Joe Brieaz with an enormous economic investment and a strong promotional strategy. This involved widespread publicity through posters, magazines, and television, aiming to launch his career. "una enorme de sembols económico y una grandísima apuesta por promocionar a Joe Brieaz se hizo una enorme promoción en cartelería en revistas en televisión en un montón de cosas."

srcs.episode: Tras los inicios del Glam. Jobriath

podcast.title: Investment in Joe Brieaz
podcast.body: Elektra Records offered Joe Brieaz a substantial contract worth half a million dollars, reflecting a significant financial commitment and a major push to promote him. This was seen as a crucial opportunity for the United States to catch up with the global glam movement, which was thriving with artists like David Bowie. "él consigue gracias a Jerry Brande un primer contrato con el extra recorso por medio millón de dólares y la verdad es que para Estados Unidos era una gran oportunidad porque con el movimiento glam y con David Bowie explotando de popularidad en todo el mundo."

srcs.episode: Tras los inicios del Glam. Jobriath

podcast.title: Kyuss Acquisition and Discontent
podcast.body: After their original indie label went out of business, Kyuss was absorbed into Elektra, a major label under the Warner Empire. The band was unhappy with this move. "Their record label went under and they got absorbed into Elektra, part of the major label Warner Empire. That didn't sit well with them."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Secrets of Queens of the Stone Age: Part 1

podcast.title: Rejection of First Album Mix
podcast.body: Elektra Records rejected the initial mix of The Stooges' self-titled debut album. The label president, Jack Holtzman, personally stepped in to remix the record before its release. "The first mix was rejected by the record label. The lecture president, Jack Holtzman, came in to do it himself."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About The Stooges?

podcast.title: Signing of The Stooges
podcast.body: Elektra Records, through talent scout Danny Fields, signed The Stooges despite the label's bosses being "absolutely stupified" by the band's unconventional sound. Fields was known for signing influential hippie bands like The Doors. "He, for example, was the guy who signed the doors. While in Detroit, to check out another bank called the MC5, Danny heard about the stuages. And even though his bosses were absolutely stupified by them, they agreed to sign the band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About The Stooges?

podcast.title: They Might Be Giants Album Release
podcast.body: Elektra Records released They Might Be Giants' album `Flood` in 1990. "they released an album entitled Flood on Electro Records."
